sections.title: Growth and identification
sections.text: Rye is a tuft-forming annual grass, usually 60–150 cm tall. Its narrow leaf blades are about 10–20 cm long and 5–10 mm wide. The flowering stem bears a single narrow spike with paired spikelets; the mature grain is an 8–10 mm caryopsis.

sections.title: Grain and uses
sections.text: Rye is a domesticated cereal cultivated for its edible grain, used for flour and bread, malt and animal feed. Grain contaminated by ergot fungus can be poisonous; that risk comes from contamination rather than normal rye grain.
